visual_brief.subject: A governed agent catalog separates approved discovery from runtime authorization
verified_context: AWS made Agent Registry generally available in GovCloud US-West for agents, tools, skills, MCP servers and custom resources.
AWS documents hybrid search, approval workflows, a native MCP endpoint and CloudTrail audit logs.
The regional launch was not independently exercised, and a registry does not by itself constrain runtime credentials, networks or tool permissions.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: Approved discovery is a catalog gate, while execution remains a separate control corridor.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: A terracotta archive of agent resources passes through one dark approval gate while a separate shadowed corridor continues beyond the catalog boundary.

candidate_notes.A: Selected. The archive, approval gate and separate dark corridor make governed discovery distinct from runtime authorization.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant, but the cabinet mass dominates the independent runtime corridor.
candidate_notes.C: Rejected before scoring because a wax-seal-like ornament introduces an unsupported ceremonial motif and weakens the operational governance idea.

crop_review.article_desktop: The archive, gate and separate corridor remain visible across the wide hero.
crop_review.article_mobile: A centered crop preserves the catalog-to-gate relationship and enough of the independent corridor to keep the control-plane distinction.
crop_review.thumbnail: The archive-and-gate silhouette remains distinct at 320px.

golden_reference_comparison: The selected image closely follows the security references' warm paper, dark containment forms and sparse terracotta wayfinding. The archive adds more repeated geometry than DNS while remaining quieter than a literal catalog diagram; Golden Reference Fit is 88.
